entries.rationale: CREATE TYPE ... FROM aliases resolve to the underlying type (commit 21762ca).

CREATE TYPE ... AS TABLE (table types / TVP shapes). Fixed: registered as CatalogTableKind.TableType; a procedure/function parameter declared with that type is bound under its own variable name, scoped to the enclosing body, so FROM @Param resolves through the same VariableTableReference path table variables use. Surfaced two further bugs while wiring this up: TableDefinition.Indexes (table-level INDEX(...) syntax, distinct from TableConstraints) was never read for ANY table, not just table types; and the predicate-side index lookup, plus five CatalogBuilder call sites (ALTER TABLE ADD/ALTER COLUMN/DROP, CREATE INDEX, CREATE COLUMNSTORE INDEX), used unscoped catalog lookups against entries that are only ever stored scoped - silently missing/misreporting for any indexed #temp table or table variable, not just TVPs. All fixed together.
CLR UDT. No visitor; a column of this type resolves Type=null - safe (UNKNOWN, never a wrong verdict). Now counted (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 0.2/3.6).
CLR assembly registration. Deliberately not modeled - coverage-remediation-plan.md decision: count and decline, never analyze CLR.

Re-points an existing CLR assembly's file/version. Same decline-to-model decision as CreateAssemblyStatement. Found by the StatementVariantParityTests reflection backstop, not by manual audit - was silently unhandled (no ledger entry at all) until this pass, unlike its CREATE sibling.
CLR aggregate. Same as CreateAssemblyStatement - counted, not analyzed.

PolyBase/external table. Column shapes live outside the scanned repo (in the external data source); resolving them would require connecting to that source, which this tool never does. Absent from the pilot corpus.

ALTER INDEX ... DISABLE/REBUILD flip CatalogIndex.IsDisabled by index name (or every index on the table for ALTER INDEX ALL), so IsIndexedColumn correctly stops/resumes counting a column as seekable. Other alter types (REORGANIZE, SET, ...) never affect seekability and are ledgered rather than modeled.
Spatial indexes support spatial predicates (STIntersects etc.), not the equality/range comparisons this tool classifies - out of scope by construction, not an oversight.
XML indexes support XQuery, not scalar comparisons - out of scope by construction.
Full-text indexes support CONTAINS/FREETEXT, not the comparison operators this tool classifies - out of scope by construction.

RETURNS @t TABLE(...) is a DeclareTableVariableBody hanging off the return type, not a DeclareTableVariableStatement, so @t was never cataloged and predicates inside the body over FROM @t were unresolvable. Fixed: registered under the function's own scope before the body is walked. A CLR TVF's RETURNS TABLE(...) has no @variable name at all (VariableName is null) - reproduced as a real NullReferenceException while building this fix, guarded, and covered by a dedicated regression test. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 3.4.

Was invisible to lineage - ViewDefinitionExtractor matched only CreateViewStatement. Fixed: matched on the same shape as CREATE, with last-definition-in-source-order-wins semantics reused from ViewDependencyGraph.TopologicalSort (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 2.1).
Same fix as AlterViewStatement - the modern SSDT idiom for redefining a view now resolves into lineage. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 2.1.
Declared RETURNS @t TABLE(...) shape resolved as Declared provenance. See MultiStatementTvfReturnVariable for the separate body-scope gap.

CatalogBuilder registers every scalar CREATE/ALTER FUNCTION's RETURNS type under its qualified name (DatabaseCatalog.AddScalarFunctionReturnType); TypedPredicateExtractor.ResolveFunctionCallOperand consults the registry for any call that isn't a curated built-in, so WHERE VarcharCol = dbo.fn_ReturnsNvarchar(@x) now types the right side and classifies normally instead of always resolving Unknown.

Was handled for catalog scoping and predicate-body walking, but not by ViewDefinitionExtractor - an ALTER FUNCTION redefining an iTVF/MSTVF was invisible to lineage. Fixed (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 2.1).
Same fix as AlterFunctionStatement. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 2.1.

A CLR TVF still declares its RETURNS TABLE(...) column list in the script even though the body is EXTERNAL NAME - unlike a CLR scalar function, there is no missing type information, so it resolves through the identical declared-shape path an ordinary multi-statement TVF uses. Not a gap; corrects an earlier (wrong) assumption in this plan that it was.
Azure ML / language-extension external function. No local body to analyze - out of scope by construction.

ViewDependencyGraph's TableReferenceCollector collected only NamedTableReference. An iTVF selecting FROM another iTVF created no dependency edge, so topo order could resolve the outer function before the inner one and its columns would degrade to Unknown; TVF cycles went undetected. Fixed: the collector also matches SchemaObjectFunctionTableReference. Verified as genuinely load-bearing by temporarily reverting the fix and confirming both regression tests fail without it. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 3.5.
AFTER/FOR DML triggers on tables, inserted/deleted resolved to the target table (commit 6534feb).
Was missing from both CatalogBuilder and TypedPredicateExtractor while procedures and functions both got all three variants - fixed (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 2.1).
Works because TriggerType is never read - the table-target path is identical for AFTER and INSTEAD OF. Correct by omission, not by design (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 5).

Was resolved via catalog.Find only; DatabaseCatalog holds no views, so every inserted/deleted predicate was dropped with the misleading reason 'has no known DDL' while the view sat fully resolved in resolvedViews. Fixed: resolvedViews is checked first. The view-derived relation's BaseColumn provenance is downgraded to Declared (FromScopeResolver.ToPseudoTableRelation(ResolvedRelation, string)) so a column that passes an indexed base column straight through the view still does not claim that index for inserted/deleted, same reasoning as the table case (Phase 1.1). coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 3.3.

Was a WRONG ANSWER, not a missing one: inserted/deleted used to resolve through the ordinary BaseColumn path and inherit Indexed=true from the target table, though inserted/deleted have no index of their own - a ScanForced+indexed finding there would have ranked first under the CLAUDE.md ranking rule while not being a real index-killing conversion. Fixed by giving pseudo-table columns Declared provenance (FromScopeResolver.ToPseudoTableRelation) - the same never-guess-an-index treatment a multi-statement TVF's declared column already gets - instead of BaseColumn. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 1.1, was the highest-priority item in the whole plan.

entries.construct: CreateTriggerStatement (DDL: ON DATABASE / ON ALL SERVER)
entries.rationale: TriggerObject.Name is null for a DDL trigger (no target table). Reproduced as an unguarded NullReferenceException that aborted the whole scan; fixed to record a ledger entry and still walk the body for ordinary predicates against real tables (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 0.3). No inserted/deleted pseudo-tables exist for this trigger kind at all (EVENTDATA() is the data source), so nothing beyond the guard is missing.
Same nameless-TriggerObject shape as the DDL-trigger case; same fix. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 0.3.

The tool only ever types comparison predicates (=, <, IN, BETWEEN). INSERT target-column/source-column mismatches and SET/assignment expressions are never type-checked - deliberately out of scope: assignment implicit conversion is a correctness concern, not the index-seek-loss concern this tool exists for.

entries.construct: WhileStatement / IfStatement boolean guard (no FROM scope)
entries.rationale: A bare IF @x = @y guard with no enclosing QuerySpecification/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE scope is dropped with a ledger entry - correct, since such a comparison can never be index-relevant.
Resolved as a view layer for depth purposes (commit 70bdc65 / audit-remediation-plan.md Phase 4.2).
Anchor branch resolved; recursive branch's contribution deliberately marked Unknown rather than guessed, and ledgered.

Works by construction - the reparsed dynamic-SQL fragment goes through the identical TypedPredicateExtractor visitor and CteResolver, no separate code path exists (coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 4.3).

Previously fell through FromScopeResolver's default arm alongside OPENROWSET/PIVOT, ledgered but unresolved - unlike those, a table variable is fully resolvable (it's cataloged, just needed a matching FROM-clause case), so it doesn't belong lumped in with the genuinely out-of-scope external/reshaping sources. Fixed as part of coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 3.4 (the MSTVF return-variable fix needed this to actually be reachable from FROM @t).

FromScopeResolver's default arm already records these to the ledger with the construct's real type name and resolves to an empty relation - the one pass in this codebase that ledgers unhandled node kinds by default rather than needing a dedicated fix per kind. Genuinely out of scope (external/reshaping sources), unlike VariableTableReference.
Reparsed script shares the same DatabaseCatalog/LineageCatalog as static SQL - full depth/origin/indexed attribution preserved.

DynamicSqlScanner records the enclosing proc/function/trigger as a DynamicSqlScope and DynamicSqlPipeline threads it through NonSargablePredicateScanner and TypedPredicateExtractor, recursing into nested dynamic SQL too - a #temp table or trigger inserted/deleted declared in the calling scope now resolves inside dynamic SQL the same way it resolves in the static body.

A nested call's own explicit argument binding (e.g. @P = @Code, where @Code is one of the enclosing script's own declared parameters) lets the enclosing type stand in when the nested call's own @params can't resolve it - deliberately narrower than full name-scope propagation, which would risk a false verdict from an unrelated same-named variable.

entries.construct: Objects created inside dynamic SQL (EXEC('CREATE TABLE #x ...'))
entries.rationale: Deliberately not resolved - feeding dynamically-created objects back into a catalog later passes have already consumed is a re-entrancy problem out of proportion to its value, and would require guessing which EXEC calls run before which. coverage-remediation-plan.md Phase 4.4.
